analysis.title: Kennametal Inc. (KMT): Raising FY27 EPS on tungsten beat, out year estimates unchanged
key_insights: KMT reported F1Q27 (Sep-26 quarter) segment EBIT of $380mn vs Visible Alpha consensus of $293mn, a +$87mn beat. GS estimates all of the beat came from better tungsten price/cost (~$95mn).
F1Q27 EPS was reported at $3.48 vs VA consensus of $2.65. Excluding the $3.09 tungsten price/cost benefit, GS estimates EPS would have been ~$0.39.

KMT raised its FY27 adj. EPS guide to $5.00-$6.00 from $4.15-$5.15 to reflect the 1Q beat. The FY27 sales guide is unchanged at $3,330mn-$3,450mn, with organic growth of ~+41% to +47% (price/volume assumption 41.5%/2.5%).
KMT introduced an F2Q27 EPS guide of $1.20-$1.50 vs consensus of $1.34.
Tungsten has corrected to ~$2,700/mtu, which raises the 2H27 price/cost headwind. KMT now expects tungsten impacts of +$1.00/-$0.55/-$2.62 in F2Q/F3Q/F4Q, vs +$0.96/-$0.39/-$2.43 previously.

Metal Cutting posted its fourth consecutive quarter of volume growth at mid-single-digit or better. Infrastructure volumes fell by a low double-digit percentage on price sensitivity and China mining weakness. KMT expects a modest Infrastructure recovery in F2Q, weighted mostly to 2H27.
F1Q27 organic growth was +54%, with Infrastructure +97% and Metal Cutting +29%.
GS raises FY27 EPS to $5.70 from $5.20. The raise is smaller than the 1Q beat because of larger tungsten headwinds in 2H27. FY28/FY29 EPS are unchanged at $2.00/$2.25.

GS views the tungsten benefit as transitory and keeps its Sell rating until KMT delivers a more meaningful volume inflection. The 12-month price target moves to $30 from $33, implying an ~8.5% FY28 FCF yield.
The target multiple on Q5-Q8 estimates falls to 8.0x from 8.5x, reflecting a broader de-rating in the space.

market_movers.rationale: Price target cut to $30 from $33 on a roll-forward and a lower target multiple (8.0x vs 8.5x). GS sees the tungsten benefit as transitory and wants a volume inflection before turning more positive.

earnings_insights: KMT F1Q27 (quarter ended Sep-26, reported 11/4-11/5): EPS $3.48 reported vs Visible Alpha consensus $2.65. Segment EBIT $380mn vs VA consensus $293mn. Organic growth +54%.
KMT FY27 adj. EPS guidance raised to $5.00-$6.00 from $4.15-$5.15. GS estimate for FY27 EPS is $5.70 (old $5.20). GS FY28E/FY29E EPS are $2.00/$2.25, unchanged.
KMT F2Q27 EPS guidance of $1.20-$1.50 vs consensus of $1.34. GS F2Q (Dec-26) EPS estimate is $1.45.
Tungsten price/cost impact guided for F2Q/F3Q/F4Q at +$1.00/-$0.55/-$2.62 (previously +$0.96/-$0.39/-$2.43). F1Q27 EPS excluding the $3.09 tungsten benefit would have been ~$0.39 (GS estimate).
risk_factors: Upside risks to the Sell rating as listed by GS: General Engineering/Transportation/Energy organic growth better than expected, stronger operating leverage, better FCF conversion.
Tungsten price corrected to ~$2,700/mtu, increasing the 2H27 price/cost headwind.
Infrastructure volumes declined on price sensitivity and China mining weakness.

tension_points.bull_case: F1Q27 EPS of $3.48 beat consensus of $2.65 and FY27 EPS guidance was raised to $5.00-$6.00. Metal Cutting has had four straight quarters of volume growth.
tension_points.bear_case: GS sees the tungsten price/cost benefit as transitory. Ex-tungsten, 1Q27 EPS would have been ~$0.39, and 2H27 tungsten headwinds grow with the price correction to ~$2,700/mtu. GS expects earnings to normalize from FY28 at $2.00 EPS.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A more meaningful volume inflection, which GS says it needs before moving off Sell.
